clue.text: Dodgy hip concerns king, being this?

definitions.text: Dodgy hip concerns king, being this?

indicators.note: something dodgy is unsound and unreliable, so the letters that follow will not stay in their printed order

parts.note: all fifteen letters of these three words are the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A monarch fretting over a bad hip wonders whether this is what he has become.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: rearrange the letters of the three middle words to get NO SPRING CHICKEN, and a king worrying about his hip is exactly that.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone no longer young is described with this idiom, and a failing joint in a monarch is a typical sign of advancing age.

clue.text: Well-known as a composer's work

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read playfully: set down in musical notes, as a composer does

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is whimsical: a composer's work is written in notes, so it is 'note-d'.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated person is commonly described with this adjective, and a melody written down in musical symbols has literally been put into notes.

clue.text: Crazy party for prison officers?

parts.note: screw is British slang for a prison warder
a ball is a formal dance party

explanation.surface: A wild knees-up thrown for the guards at a jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'party for prison officers' as a dance held for screws, which is a screw ball. Screw is British prison slang for a warder.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric, zany person or idea is called this, so as an adjective it means wildly odd or mad.

clue.text: Head of espionage to probe commie grass

indicators.note: a probe goes inside something, so this letter is pushed into the middle of the next word

parts.note: red is slang for a communist

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of the following word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of espionage

explanation.surface: A spymaster sent to investigate a communist who is acting as an informer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like the informer of the spy story, but here it means the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall water-loving plants with hollow stems are a kind of grass, so this plant is a fair example.

clue.text: The kind of contract that many left-wing Americans desire?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in bridge, a contract played with no suit as trumps

definitions.note: a cryptic, whimsical second meaning: what they want is no Trump
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read playfully: a wish for a certain president to be gone

explanation.surface: Progressive American voters wish for a particular kind of agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: In contract bridge, a bid can be made with no suit acting as trumps; the clue pretends the phrase is a political wish to be rid of Donald Trump.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridge players call a bid without any trump suit by this name, and it is a type of contract in that card game.

clue.text: Climber and soldiers look cold on ascent

indicators.note: in a down clue, ascending means reading from bottom to top, so the assembled string is turned around

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
to peer is to look closely
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Troops on a mountain climb glance at the cold as they go up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' sounds like a mountaineer to go with the soldiers' ascent, but it is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that grows up walls or trees by clinging to them is a climbing plant, also called by this name.

clue.text: Feeling of irritation in chest is awful

indicators.note: awful suggests something in a bad state, so the letters before it are badly jumbled

parts.note: these three words together supply the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An irritating sensation in your chest is horrible.
explanation.definitionFit: An urge to scratch an irritated skin is that state, so the feeling of irritation names it as a sensation.

clue.text: Tree-hugger fine about hugging a laurel finally

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for fine is read in the opposite direction
to hug is to wrap your arms around something, so the first piece goes around the others

parts.note: A-OK is American slang for fine, all in order
taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the final letter of laurel

explanation.surface: An environmental protester is all right with embracing a laurel tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tree-hugger' looks like an eco-campaigner, but it is the animal that clings to eucalyptus trees.
explanation.definitionFit: This Australian marsupial spends its life clinging to eucalyptus trunks and branches, so it literally hugs trees.

clue.text: Those from whom relative may receive post?

definitions.text: Those from whom relative may receive post?

parts.words: Those from whom relative may receive post
parts.note: surface reading: people who send letters to a family member
setter's reading: post means a job, handed to a relation out of favouritism

explanation.surface: Who might send mail to a family member?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like letters in the mail, but it is a job: these people hand jobs to their relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: People who show favouritism to family by giving them positions of power or employment are known by this term.

clue.text: Up-for-lease houses close to clear stream

indicators.note: to house something is to hold it inside, so the next letter goes within the phrase for available to let

parts.note: a property up for lease is available to rent

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its last letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of clear

explanation.surface: Rental properties sit next to a clear brook.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast, violent flow of water is a kind of stream, here used as the noun for a rushing current.

clue.text: Grip fiddled with lens cap

indicators.note: fiddling with something means messing it about, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: both words supply the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A photographer holds tight while fidgeting with the cover of a camera lens.
explanation.definitionFit: To clasp something firmly in your hands or arms is to hold or grip it tightly.

clue.text: Unhappy private duke sent to the front

indicators.note: being sent to the front means this letter is placed at the start, before the other piece

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
your own room is a private one

explanation.surface: A miserable soldier because a nobleman has been posted to the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like a soldier to match 'sent to the front', but it is an adjective meaning personal.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low or depressed is described as feeling this way, a common informal synonym for sad.

clue.text: Can pupils cross by end of street, one asks

indicators.note: by means next to, so the extra letter is placed alongside the rearranged ones
cross means angry, and the letters in a temper are thrown into disorder

parts.note: both words supply nine letters to rearrange

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the final letter of street

explanation.surface: Children wonder whether they may walk across the road at the end of the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who humbly begs or petitions for something is a petitioner, someone who asks.

clue.text: Big change for small headline in Fish Monthly?

parts.note: surface reading: a major reorganisation

parts.words: for small headline in Fish Monthly?
parts.note: setter's reading: a fishing magazine headline announcing that the number of small hake has risen, S for small, the fish, and 'up'

explanation.surface: A dramatic overhaul at an angling magazine, starting with a tiny headline.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as S HAKE UP: a headline in a fish paper reporting that small hake are up. Hake is a sea fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A major reorganisation of a company or team, in which roles are shuffled, is called by this hyphenated noun.

clue.text: Uncompromising series on hospital department

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another means it sits above it, so the first word is placed before the second

parts.note: a string of events is a series
ENT is Ear, Nose and Throat

explanation.surface: A tough-minded run of programmes about a hospital unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Rules that are strict and exacting, allowing no leniency, are described with this adjective.

clue.text: Neat prose could be translated into this

definitions.text: Neat prose could be translated into this

indicators.note: translating changes the form of words, so these letters may be rearranged into another form

parts.note: both words supply nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Elegant writing might be rendered into some other language.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: rearranging the first two words gives the language, and any prose can indeed be translated into it.
explanation.definitionFit: This invented international language was designed so that writing from any tongue could be rendered into it.

clue.text: River policemen powerless to net anglers?

indicators.note: P stands for power, so being powerless means that letter is taken away

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river
peelers is an old British name for police officers, after Sir Robert Peel

explanation.surface: River police without authority try to catch some fishermen.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as playful: anglers reel in their catch, so they could be called this.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishermen wind in their lines with a reel, so a whimsical name for them is people who reel.

clue.text: Coming endless crisis? Not the last for EU

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: an emergency is a crisis

indicators.note: not the last tells you to drop the final letter of the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Is a never-ending crisis looming? Not the final one for the European Union.
explanation.definitionFit: The process of appearing or coming out into view is this noun, so it matches 'coming' used as a noun.

clue.text: Turning more pasty, starts to sicken experiencing this

definitions.text: Turning more pasty, starts to sicken experiencing this

indicators.note: turning means the word goes the other way round, read from its end

parts.note: pasty means pale-faced, so more pasty is paler

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters, so only the openings of the next two words are used

parts.note: the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone going greyer in the face is falling ill again.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a recovering patient who goes pale and starts to sicken is going through a relapse.
explanation.definitionFit: Falling ill again after seeming to recover is this setback, which pallor and sickness typically signal.

clue.text: Heel finally heals after nurse gets involved

indicators.note: after means placed later, so the earlier pieces follow the word for nurse

parts.note: EN is an Enrolled Nurse
a ship that heels leans over, or lists

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word after it

parts.note: the final letter of heals

explanation.surface: A patient's heel finally mends once a nurse takes part in the treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heel' looks like the foot, but it is the verb for a ship leaning over.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign up or join in with something, such as the army or a cause, is to become involved in it.

clue.text: Small store ultimately cuts prices for Pampers

indicators.note: cutting into something means going inside it, so these letters break into the word for prices

parts.note: costs are prices
S is the abbreviation for small

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so the last letter of the preceding word is used

parts.note: the final letter of store

explanation.surface: A little shop eventually reduces the price of a well-known nappy brand.
explanation.walkthrough: Pampers is a brand of nappies, which fits the shop picture, but here it is a verb meaning spoils.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat someone with excessive indulgence and care is to spoil or coddle them, which is what pampering means.

clue.text: Bag up aristocrat's discarded garment

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading from bottom to top, so the word for bag is turned around

parts.note: a sac is a bag-like pouch
toff is British slang for an upper-class person

explanation.surface: Pack up the nobleman's old clothes that he has thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing that someone no longer wants and has handed on or thrown out is called by this term.

clue.text: A line crossed by nudist in Darwin?

indicators.note: crossed by means having something go across and around it, so the short pieces sit inside the word for nudist

parts.note: a naturist is a nudist
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Was there a single naked person in the Australian city of Darwin?
explanation.walkthrough: Darwin looks like the city in northern Australia, but it is Charles Darwin; the question mark marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Darwin studied plants and animals in the field, making him a famous example of a student of nature.

clue.text: Sweet energy drink brought round to take on run

indicators.note: bringing something round turns it to face the other way, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy

indicators.note: taking something on means accepting it inside, so the letter for run is put into the middle

parts.note: a tot is a small drink of spirits
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A sugary energy drink is handed around before setting off on a jog.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich layered cake served as a dessert is this, and a dessert is called a sweet in Britain.

clue.text: Some big bonnie people abroad

indicators.note: some means a portion only, so the letters are a run taken from inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: A few large, pretty folk living overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: Bonnie is a Scottish word for pretty.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a major ethnic group of south-eastern Nigeria, so they are a people living in a foreign land.

clue.text: Sullen following of leader creates a stink

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the word for sullen is placed behind the other letter
the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of of
dour means sullen and gloomy

explanation.surface: A grumpy group of followers kicks up a fuss about their boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A stink' sounds like a fuss or row, but here it is a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A smell, especially an unpleasant one, is this noun, so a stink is a strong bad smell.

clue.text: Slight sirens luring transports

indicators.note: a transport carries something inside it, so the letters are carried within the words before it

parts.note: the letters span the join of these two words

explanation.surface: Seductive sirens tempting sailors carry them away a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight' looks like an adjective meaning small, but it is a noun meaning an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: An insulting remark that damages someone's reputation is a slur, and a slight is a similar insult or snub.

clue.text: Limits restricting republican artist's commissions

indicators.note: to restrict is to confine, so the following letters are held inside the word for limits

parts.note: ends are limits
R is the abbreviation for republican
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: Boundaries curb the paid work an anti-monarchist painter is given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commissions' looks like paid artistic work to suit the artist, but it means tasks one is sent on.
explanation.definitionFit: Small tasks someone is asked to carry out, such as going to the shops, are jobs given to them.

clue.text: Men network at party in southeastern city

parts.note: OR is Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers
LAN is a Local Area Network
a do is a party, and at here just places the men at it

explanation.surface: Guys networking at a social event in some city in the south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: This Florida city, home of Disney World, lies in the southeastern United States.

clue.text: Shabby drunk

definitions.meaning: first meaning: worn and damaged by use
second meaning: in a poor state through drink

explanation.walkthrough: Two words that look like a description of one tramp are two separate meanings of the same phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something worn out by long use, and humorously a person in poor shape after heavy drinking.
